howto.name: Add the Word document
howto.text: Drop or select a .docx file up to 500 MB. Older .doc files are not accepted here; Office to PDF handles a wider range of formats.

howto.name: Convert to PDF
howto.text: Run the conversion. The text of each paragraph is set in Helvetica on A4 pages with 1-inch margins, and headings become larger bold text. Images, tables, equations, headers, footers and links are left out.

howto.name: Download and check the PDF
howto.text: Open the PDF and check it: everything is set in one typeface, any text that was in tables, text boxes, headers or footers is missing, and so is every equation.

faq.q: Will the PDF look exactly like my Word document?
faq.a: No. Only the text of the body paragraphs is carried over, in Helvetica on A4 pages; headings are enlarged and bold, and a paragraph with any bold or italic text is set that way throughout. Fonts, alignment, spacing, images, tables, equations, headers, footers and links are not kept. For a close copy of the layout, use Office to PDF, which converts with LibreOffice.

No. Word keeps an equation apart from the text of its paragraph, and only that text is carried over, so each equation is left out and the words around it close up: a line reading "Before x/y after.", with x/y as an equation, comes out as "Before after." The result says how many equations were left out. Office to PDF keeps Word equations.

faq.q: Why do the fonts look different?
faq.a: Because every paragraph is set in Helvetica, whatever fonts the document uses, and characters outside Western European scripts, such as Cyrillic or Chinese, do not print correctly. Office to PDF keeps the document's fonts where the server has them.

faq.q: Which file types can I convert?
faq.a: This page takes .docx. For .doc, .odt, .rtf, spreadsheets or presentations, use Office to PDF, which accepts a wider set of formats.

faq.q: Are comments and tracked changes included?
faq.a: Accept or reject tracked changes and remove comments before converting if you do not want them to appear. Converting exactly the version you intend to share avoids surprises.

faq.q: Do links and headings carry over?
faq.a: Headings do, as larger bold text: Heading 1 and 2 get their own sizes, and lower levels share a third. Links do not: their text is kept but is not clickable, and a table of contents comes across as plain text.

faq.q: What happens to my document after I upload it?
faq.a: It is uploaded over HTTPS and converted on the PrivaTools server in isolated temporary per-request storage, using local libraries rather than a third-party service. Response cleanup removes the document and the PDF and the result after your download is sent, and a background sweep clears anything an interrupted request leaves behind. Nothing is added to an account or file library.
